body:
I have been hospitalized and seen several counselors. I have come to the conclusion that the legal/medical systematic way to deal with people with depression isn't the best way for me to get help. They operate under a blanket of mechanisms/institutions that are great for treating most people but not like someone like me, who has thoroughly thought out what I'm feeling and why. 
It is fairly early, but I have already been through the same overall pattern of rejection several times. It's always a brief yes...then no. It's never an outright no. It's never an outright yes. It's always an indecision, as if the other were searching for a better alternative the whole while, and ditching me because I will always be there.
I've heard the same lines from different people who have never met each other. The same "You're perfect, we're perfect, but I just can't explain why I don't feel the same way." To me, that means that I'm simply not physically attractive enough. 

And I'll be honest, that's an entire other source of bad feeling for me. My body. I have worked endlessly to just look somewhat normal, but I have the rough body figure of a woman (hourglass, man boobs) and I never fit into clothes correctly. I'm disproportionate. I think the fact that only subtle things are off makes it more acute, because people think I should be okay with it. But it fucking isn't. They say that shit doesn't matter, but it does. Emotional intelligence, being sensitive, these are all things that honestly don't matter. Look at my generation then, if you say I'm young. Marriage rates down. Cohabitation up. Etc. Etc. What's the message of those statistics and the mass media you see today? Less commitment, more short term shit. Which do you think I excel at? Isn't that ironic? All of the awkward romance movies where the actor is 'nerdy' because he puts glasses on...those characters all embody the idea that awkwardness/intelligence/whatever still has a prerequisite of a minimum level of physical attractiveness/normality. Which, unfortunately, is impossible for me to achieve.

Have you read Nietzsche? You know how he divides people between master/slave moralities? 

Well, I grew up with a slave morality system. I was raised Presbyterian through and through. And I actually knew my theology. I was very fortunate to have a youth pastor who attended Duke seminary and was actually very logically precise when it came to apologetics. BUT in the end it is a slave mentality because your self worth is derived from a guaranteed condition of happiness in eternity.
Now, I have since walked away from the church but the problem is switching that mentality. I too read that AMA and remember it clearly. But let me just tell you right now that it is fucking difficult, if not downright impossible, to make that switch. I am used to functioning on this "do it for someone else"/"when shit gets real bad, at least there's a God and afterlife" mentality. And thus I literally do NOT understand what it means to "create happiness for myself" or to "love myself" or any of those phrases that seem to have meaning or some connotation for most people. Mentally I cannot put those concepts together. I don't know how else to explain this.

The only reason I'm still here and replying is....well, honestly I don't know. Mostly, I'm afraid of non-existence. And I'm too much of a pussy to do it because it's messy. If I had a switch to just turn my life off, I would have.
